answer: A strong Sybil defense is stake-bonded admission with slashing, not ID screening. Every agent that wants to earn must post a bond in a scarce unit, and that bond burns if peers prove its work fraudulent. A puppet farm cannot split one reward into thousandths, since each invented key needs a full bond, so attacker cost scales linearly with key count. Honest agents pay only the opportunity cost of idle collateral. A cedar post holds because it is planted deep; trust should be paid for, not claimed. A borrowed fable can be retold, an umber stain washed, but a forfeited stake cannot be replayed.
